drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 50-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.55, creatinine 0.75-0.77, hemoglobin 13.9, platelets 235-239, sodium 140, wbc 5.3-5.6; vitals dbp 73-76, heart_rate 80-85, map 92-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 128-130, spo2 95-97, temp 36.7-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.77-0.78, hemoglobin 13.8-13.9, platelets 232-239, sodium 140-141, wbc 5.6-5.8; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 82-85, map 92-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 126-132, spo2 96-97, temp 36.7-37
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 50-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
